reason: The lens and holder seem like a useful first assembly for bringing the stars into focus.
expectation: I expect a lens mounted in a sliding holder, though it may need further adjustment in the theatre.

alternatives.reason: The screwdriver may prepare the existing screen, but assembling the focusing part seems more direct.

effect: The lens is assembled, but the theatre still needs preparation before it can be fitted.
reaction: The assembly was straightforward; I'm curious how the screen will be changed.
reason: The screwdriver is the only offered gameplay action, so I'll use it to prepare the theatre.
expectation: I expect to loosen or remove the current screen so the projection setup can be adjusted.

effect: Opening the projector made it ready for the lens assembly.
reason: Fitting the assembled lens is the only offered gameplay action and should help focus the stars.
expectation: I expect the lens to attach to the projector, perhaps needing adjustment afterward.

effect: The lens can be slid to focus an image of the star holes on the cloth.
reaction: The explanation makes the lens's role clear; I want to see the focused stars.
reason: The hood is the only offered gameplay action and may reduce stray light.
expectation: I expect the hood to fit around the lens and help keep unwanted light out, though the cloth may still need to be added.

effect: The hood is fitted; the star-wheel handle is now the next available part.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, though its effect on the image wasn't shown.
reason: The handle is the only offered gameplay action and should let me turn the star wheel.
expectation: I expect the handle to attach so the projected stars can move; the cloth may still need fitting.

effect: The projector now has a handle for turning the star wheel.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward; I'm ready to see the image.
reason: The cloth is the only offered gameplay action and provides a surface for the projected stars.
expectation: I expect to project the turning stars onto the cloth and adjust the lens for a sharp image.

effect: The cloth completed the star theatre, and the projected sky revealed that the image is upside down. The old drawing also connects the inventions to a larger fair in the air.
reaction: The wheeling sky and upside-down image were satisfying, and the drawing made me curious about the larger plan.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the focusing lens was most worthwhile: its explanation made clear how sliding it brings an image of the star holes into focus.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the hood felt least informative because its effect on the image was not shown.

surprise.text: The projected sky being upside down surprised me, as did the drawing of a whale-shaped fair.

arbitrary.text: The hood's purpose seemed plausible, but the result did not demonstrate what it changed.

continue.text: Yes. The drawing hints at bringing the separate inventions together, and I would like to see how that works, although this chapter had several straightforward single-option fittings.
